title: Rework variable and API checks to suppress httr exception.
description:
### Problem:

Generation of the warning messages involves a number of logical checks, which includes an API call to the RStudio Connect server using the `httr` package. If the httr GET call throws an exception, the entire generation of the user-manual is aborted, resulting in a generic error displayed on the RStudio Connect server:

![2021-07-28 at 8 37 AM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/17675905/127352300-3f74e3f8-be00-45bc-b58d-8e7fcb396dfa.jpg)

This is reproducible within the development environment because of an issue with httr and the self-signed certificates present within the RStudio Connect development environment.

In addition, formatting enhancements are desired for the warning message output.

### Solution:

I have reworked the generation of the `warning_message` function to catch any exceptions that occur within the `httr` GET call and display the error with any other failed checks. The logic as also been reworked to always succeed, while providing additional diagnostics with the `DEBUGME` package (and better resolution hints for the warnings themselves). In addition, the ability to specify an environment variable `PLUMBERTABLEAU_USE_HTTP` = TRUE which will allow a work-around for the self-signed certificates by downgrading a `https` server address to `http`. 

Without this environment variable defined (within RStudio Connect's application settings):

![2021-07-28 at 8 49 AM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/17675905/127354428-c49d35be-03c4-4957-8738-ca6a85061a4a.jpg)

With this environment variable defined (within RStudio Connect's application settings):
![2021-07-28 at 8 50 AM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/17675905/127354547-ee56f3c3-d7a2-48e2-9ef1-1b427ac56f71.jpg)

I've also adjusted the formatting of the warning messages. With several warning messages activated, this is what it looks like:

![2021-07-28 at 2 22 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/17675905/127397909-480fdc86-62a5-4bb5-8bf0-bf2677836ebd.jpg)

title: Documentation Changes
description: This PR was in draft form for a while so we could easily diff changes.

title: Documentation
description: Adding package documentation, mainly vignettes and articles

title: Adding some more unit tests
description:
This PR adds tests for the usage instructions (as a snapshot test) and `write_log_message()`.

It's based on #44, so it looks right now like it includes more changes than it actually does. Because of this, I might redo this PR if it doesn't look a lot cleaner once #44 has been merged.

title: Code reorganization and minor misc changes
description:
- Moved `warning_message()` and `info_message()` to their own `messages.R` file.
- Created `plumbertableau-package.R` so that `?plumbertableau` shows package-level help.
- Moved `parseQS()` and `combine_keys()` to `reroute.R`.
- Minor update to `README.md`
- Minor updates to test descriptions to name the functions they describe.

title: Tests, code re-org, other small changes from package review
description:
This PR contains some small updates from my review of the package and its tests:

- Add dependencies to the `DESCRIPTION` following @blairj09’s parallel branch.
- Moved some functions out of `utils.R`. I moved functions that were used in one part of the code, especially if they seemed to be a core part of that functionality.
    - The functions to generate messages went into `openapi.R`
    - `parseQS()` and `combine_keys()` went into `reroute.R`.
- I updated some error messages in `tableau_handler.R`.
- Added a test to `test-tableau_json.R` to complete its coverage.

title: UI/UX Updates
description:
This PR is based on feedback from @jcheng5 and introduces a number of changes:

- Whenever an extension is published to RStudio Connect and the RStudio Connect environment doesn't support it, for any reason, we display a warning page instead of the standard Tableau Usage guide. The warnings page is rough right now, but I think it's a start:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/10444878/125139601-0ebbb700-e0ce-11eb-9d8e-55876b8f9db4.png)

- The OpenAPI description field has been dramatically simplified

title: Better programmatic development of Tableau extensions
description:
This alters `tableau_extension()` to modify the router, rather than _returning a function to modify the router_. It also moves `warnings` to an option (`plumbertableau.warnings`). This doesn't alter the standard user experience that much (use `tableau_extension` instead of `tableau_extension()`) but it makes it much more intuitive to programmatically create Tableau extensions.

Closes #35

title: Add tests for `reroute()`
description:
This PR adds some tests for for `reroute()`, implemented with mocked-up request objects.

The tests themselves test the rewriting the `PATH_INFO` property requests to "/evaluate", returning the info list object for requests to the "/info" endpoint, and returning `1L` in the appropriate circumstances.

To mock up the request objects, I used the `make_req` function, which I copied over from Plumber's test helpers.

To make things work, I had to modify the `encode_payload()` function to optionally skip encoding the JSON payload as raw bytes, otherwise `reroute` failed, expecting the `postBody` property to be text rather than raw. I _guess_ this is probably because in use, the Plumber router would have decoded the body before `reroute` encountered it? This might speak to some of the advantages of using the test-in-situ approach: using mocked requests, we need to mock up the request in whatever state the function expects it.

Running swagger Docs at http://127.0.0.1:5762/__docs__/

title: RStudio Connect updates
description:
This updates the package to work with the new changes on RStudio Connect. Namely, RStudio Connect forwards the exact requests from Tableau, rather than modifying the request. This allows all request modifications to be handled directly in `plumbertableau`.

There are a few challenges here:
* I don't think there's any way around checking for whether or not the router is running on RStudio Connect. This is because RStudio Connect handles the vanity path, and when the router is running on RStudio Connect then `plumbertableau` shouldn't inject the vanity path. Otherwise, it ends up duplicated and you end up with paths like `.../stringutils/stringutils/capitalize`
* The Tableau user-guide relies on the route path to build out the user guide. However, on RSC this path is incomplete since it's missing the vanity URL:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/10444878/118077519-775a1200-b371-11eb-8f33-c6a2b6de0adf.png)

We'll need to adjust how the user-guide path is generated so it accurately reflects the full path

title: Provide default parser and serializer and warn users not to change them

title: Use Roxygen-style comments for Tableau metadata
Update validate_request to handle tableau_arg_spec objects
description: This fixes a bug that caused endpoints that used `arg_spec()` to fail with odd errors. The bug was due to the fact that we were checking for a straight match between the expected data type and the provided data type. This works when `arg_spec()` isn't used, because the definition of expected types is just a list. However, when `arg_spec()` is used, the resulting list is a list of `tableau_arg_spec` objects, which need to be compared differently.

title: Tableau request validation
description:
This PR uses `validate_request()` to allow a user to validate an incoming Tableau request. The current checks that are implemented are:
* Verify the number of values passed from Tableau matches the expected number of values
* Check the data type of the Tableau values against expected data types

The response returned from the API can be properly presented to the user in Tableau:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/10444878/109080117-4268e800-76bd-11eb-8054-6e5ea77b5942.png)

This PR also introduces a default error handler that surfaces Plumber errors in a way that complies with Tableau's expectations.

Closes #12

Tableau OpenAPI Specification
description:
Closes #3 

This adds in OpenAPI specification details so that swagger (or whatever UI is used) provides users with a template for how Tableau submits data to the API. This allows users to verify API behavior directly from within RStudio w/o needing to submit an actual request from Tableau.

title: Arg parsing
description:
Closes #6 

There are a few things to note here:
* Tableau doesn't pass named values in `data`. Every value is `_arg1`, `_arg2`, ... , `_argN`
* This means arguments are passed to the function by **order** and not by name. While this may be un "R-centric", it seems no different from a developer specifically calling `body$data$`_arg1` within a router, since there's not true indication of what `_arg1` is actually referring to.
